import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')
      res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache')
      const content = readFileSync(file)
      if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') {
        const html = content.toString()
        res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}</body>`) : html + livePreviewScript)
      } else res.end(content)
    } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') }
  })
  server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() })
  server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0')
  return server
}
if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) await start()

import { startForCapture } from './capture-start.mjs'
import captures from './wip-screenshots.cjs'
import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { readFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
captures.instrument({ chromium })
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, process.platform === 'darwin' ? 'metal.json' : 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
if (process.platform === 'linux') process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()
const url = process.env.CAPTURE_URL, output = process.env.CAPTURE_DIR
if (!url || !output) throw new Error('Set CAPTURE_URL and CAPTURE_DIR.')
mkdirSync(output, { recursive: true })
const transient = error => { throw Object.assign(error, { exitCode: 75 }) }
let browser
try {
  browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions, timeout: 30000 }).catch(transient)
  for (const [name, width, height] of [['desktop', 1440, 900], ['mobile', 390, 844]]) {
    const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width, height } }).catch(transient)
    page.setDefaultTimeout(30000)
    const failures = []
    page.on('pageerror', error => { console.error(error.message); failures.push(error.message) })
    page.on('response', response => { if (response.status() >= 400 && new URL(response.url()).origin === new URL(url).origin) failures.push(`HTTP ${response.status()}: ${response.url()}`) })
    const response = await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 45000 }).catch(transient)
    if (!response?.ok()) throw Object.assign(new Error(`HTTP ${response?.status()} loading preview`), { exitCode: !response || [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504].includes(response.status()) ? 75 : 1 })
    await page.locator(process.env.CAPTURE_READY_SELECTOR || 'body').waitFor({ state: 'visible' })
    await page.waitForFunction(() => document.fonts.status === 'loaded')
    const start = await startForCapture(page, {
      enabled: process.env.CAPTURE_AUTO_START !== 'false',
      selector: process.env.CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR || ''
    })
    console.log(`Capture ${name}: auto-start ${start.clicked ? 'clicked' : start.reason}`)
    await page.waitForTimeout(1000)
    await page.screenshot({ path: join(output, `final-${name}.png`), timeout: 30000 }).catch(error => {
      if (error.name === 'TimeoutError' || !browser.isConnected()) transient(error)
      throw error
    })
    if (process.env.CAPTURE_STRICT === '1' && failures.length) throw new Error(`Published build failed: ${failures.join('; ')}`)
    await page.close()
  }
} catch (error) { console.error(error); process.exitCode = error.exitCode || 1 }
finally { await browser?.close().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode ||= 75 }) }

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from

inspecting the runner.

# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? --- I want you to build a first-person shooter at the level of the most recent Call of Duty games. It should be utterly perfect, visually beautiful, with every single thing done at AAA quality—from textures to physics to anything you could think of. Fan out sub-agents and have sub-agents tackle each one individually so that the game is utterly perfect. Have a separate sub-agent check each item visually to ensure it looks triple A. That separate sub-agent should be a really harsh critic, and if it doesn't look triple A, keep iterating until it does. Don't stop until each sub-agent is utterly wowed with the quality when compared with the actual Call of Duty game. It should literally compare them side by side blind and say which one looks better. Do this in ThreeJS. Continue iterating until it's utterly perfect. Fan out sub-agents and ultracode. /home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime/ideas: github-actions-visual-workflow-editor.md github-agent-project-comparison.md ios-builder-native-app-generation.md issue-triggered-opencode-workflow.md live-source-file-browser.md omgithub-self-hosted-supabase-migration.md opencode-docker-sandbox.md opencode-oauth-env-auth.md opencode-token-isolation.md remix-preview-port-ownership.md /home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime/wiki: access.md opencode-v2-experiment.md opencode.md testing.md

The prompt.md is an example giant prompt (FPS COD). The actual user prompt is "GTA-style 3D open world on bikes". We should build a great game. Let's use Three.js via Vite.

Let me plan the implementation carefully, then write files.

Architecture:
- package.json: vite, three.
- index.html: full-screen canvas, HUD in HTML/CSS, title screen.
- src/main.js: game logic.
- Maybe split modules: world.js, bike.js, traffic.js, hud.js, audio.js, missions.js. Better maintainability. But single-file can be huge. Let's make a few modules to keep readable.

Game design details:

World:
- Grid: N=10 blocks, block size 56 (building lot + sidewalks), road width 16. Spacing = 72. City spans ~720. Use city blocks at coordinates (i - (N-1)/2)*spacing.
- Roads: X roads at multiples, Z roads.
- Ground: large plane colored dark asphalt; blocks: raised sidewalk slabs (light concrete) with buildings on top.
- Buildings: InstancedMesh boxes with window texture (canvas generated). Height random 18-90, width/depth nearly block size minus margins. Some downtown taller near center. Colors grayscale variations tinted via instanceColor. Use MeshStandardMaterial with canvas texture windows, emissive windows for night, but instanced texture repeated based on box UV? Box geometry UV maps each face 0-1, texture repeat not per instance. Use texture repeat (2,4) will tile windows; height variation stretches. Acceptable. Or generate 3-4 building materials/meshes with different heights? Simple approach: one InstancedMesh with texture repeat 2x4 and per-instance color; window pattern scales with building height, looks okay-ish. To improve, use shader modifying UV by instance scale? Could use onBeforeCompile to add per-instance scaling so windows stay square: custom attribute aSize. Simpler: make buildings from BoxGeometry with texture where each face UV scaled by dimensions per instance using a custom shader chunk. Might be overkill; but quality matters.

Alternative: Build buildings as merged geometry with custom UVs scaled by size (windows constant size). Use BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries for ~150 buildings, one draw call, windows tile correctly. Generate BoxGeometry per building with width/depth/height, set UVs per face scaled to world dims (u = x/3, v = y/3). Setting UVs for BoxGeometry faces: each face has uv 0..1; multiply u by width or depth, v by height. Could apply texture repeat & offset per-face via geometry attributes; texture with wrapping repeat. Merging keeps UVs. Great. Then one material with map window texture, repeat wrapping. Emissive map maybe same texture with emissive windows at night — need separate map where windows bright. Could just use one texture with emissive property; at night raise material.emissiveIntensity with emissiveMap = windowMap (windows glow). Nice.

- Streets: road markings via instanced white boxes (thin planes) along lanes, dashed center lines. Or a canvas texture for whole ground? World is 800x800, texture repeat road grid drawn procedurally would need alignment. Easiest: add dashed lane markings as merged thin boxes at y=0.02 on each road, center line and lane edges. Also crosswalks at intersections maybe.
- Sidewalk curbs: blocks are raised 0.25 with concrete color; add curb edges darker? Box slabs.
- Props: street lamps (cylinder + glowing sphere) instanced at intersections; palm trees (trunk + leaf cones) maybe; traffic lights; billboards with neon text? Neon signs add GTA vibe. Add a few billboards with canvas text ("VICE CITY", "OMG FM", "NEON RIDER") on building sides? Could add as planes attached randomly. Nice flavor.
- Park areas: some blocks are parks with grass, trees, benches. Maybe 2-3 blocks.
- Water/harbor at edge? Could be nice but keep city within.

Sky: gradient shader dome + sun, clouds? Use Scene background via canvas gradient texture? A skydome with ShaderMaterial gradient, plus fog. Time of day cycle over 4 minutes: sun position, sky colors interpolated (day → sunset → night → day); car headlights, lamp lights at night, building emissive. This adds polish. But shadow update and lighting adjustments.

Maybe keep fixed golden-hour look for best visuals (sunset city). GTA Vice City vibe: pink/orange sky, teal shadows. A "golden hour" static scene is visually striking and simpler. Day/night toggle could be extra. I'd do a slow time-of-day cycle but default at dusk; player can press T to toggle time quickly? Time cycle adds complexity but manageable. Let's implement a day-night cycle with duration 240s, starting at dusk-ish; lights computed. Might risk looking bad at night. I'll tune.

Bike physics:
- Use kinematic model on XZ plane. State: pos (Vector3), heading (yaw), speed, steering, lean, vertical velocity for jumps (ramps? curb hops). Ground flat; curbs 0.25 — ignore vertical, keep bike at y=0.15.
- Input: throttle (W/Up), brake (S/Down), steer (A/D), handbrake (Space), boost (Shift).
- accel ~22 units/s², max speed 42 (~150 km/h display scale), boost 58, reverse max -8.
- steering: yaw rate proportional to steer * speed factor, reduced at high speed, increases at low. lean visual = -steer * speed factor up to 25°, plus pitch on accel.
- grip/drift: velocity direction lags heading; implement simple slip: maintain velocity vector, lateral friction. GTA arcade: pos moves along heading; drift when handbrake reduces lateral grip. Implement velocity vector v (x,z), forward f. Decompose v into forward/lateral; lateral *= exp(-grip*dt), grip lower with handbrake. Add engine force along forward. Steering rotates heading. This gives natural drift.
- collisions: building AABBs; circle vs AABB resolve, reduce speed, shake, sparks. Also static props (lamps) maybe ignore. City boundary. Traffic cars circle/AABB collisions push and slow. Pedestrians knocked (ragdoll-ish simple tween) but maybe avoid violence? GTA style could include but let's keep peds that dive away; hitting them raises heat. Could be fine but maybe simplify: peds walk sidewalks and flee when near; hitting them = "near miss" score? Hmm.

Missions:
- "DELIVERY" mode: each checkpoint is a glowing ring/gate. HUD arrow points to next. Time bonus. Collect 10 to complete contract, cash + wanted.
- Maybe two modes: free roam + delivery contracts. Simple: checkpoints always active, collect to earn cash, each new delivery farther away, timer 60s per target, streak multiplier. On timeout, streak resets. That's engaging.
- Add ramps for jumps? Maybe place a few ramps (wedge geometry) on roads and allow simple air time with vertical physics. Nice. Implement ground height sampling: ramp boxes with slope; compute y based on ramp region. Could complicate. Maybe include jump ramps with simple trigger: when crossing ramp, gain vertical velocity based on speed, then gravity. Bike y follows ground (0) + air. Visual pitch. Adds fun.

Wanted level/police: When heat accumulates (crashing into cars, speeding, hitting peds), wanted stars 1-5. Cops on bikes spawn and chase; if they touch you, you get busted (respawn, lose cash). This is a big feature but doable with simple AI. Might be fun and GTA-like. Time constraints? I have plenty. Let's implement a light version: police bike spawn at wanted>=2, chases using same bike physics simplified (steer toward player), red/blue flashing lights; contact causes damage/busted. But under CPU rendering, extra complexity okay.

HUD:
- Top-left: cash, mission info, wanted stars.
- Bottom-right: speedometer arc gauge (canvas), gear? Speed number km/h, boost bar.
- Bottom-left minimap canvas: top-down city map (roads/blocks), player arrow, checkpoints, cops, traffic. North indicator.
- Center prompts: "FOLLOW THE ARROW", checkpoint distance, timer.
- Start screen overlay: title "NEON RIDER" / "MIDNIGHT RUN", subtitle "GTA-style open world on two wheels", controls, START RIDE button. Loading screen? Since textures procedural no loading.
- Pause on Escape with overlay. Mute button.
- Damage/health: crashes reduce health; at 0 respawn "WRECKED". Maybe health regen? Add health 100, crash damage, repair at checkpoints? Keep simple.

Audio:
- WebAudio engine: two saw oscillators + lowpass, frequency mapped to speed with wobble; tire noise filtered noise when drifting; impact thuds; pickup chime. Start on user gesture. Add mute key M and button. This adds a lot of immersion. Implement carefully with AudioContext; avoid errors.

Rendering/perf:
- Renderer antialias, shadows (PCFSoft) with directional light shadow camera 120 units following player. Buildings castShadow (merged mesh) receives. Ground receive. Instanced lamps maybe no shadows. Renderer pixelRatio min(devicePixelRatio, 1.6) maybe CPU software rendering → lower (1). Use adaptive resolution? For capture 1440x900 on SwiftShader, heavy scene could be slow. Ensure decent fps. Limit draw calls: merged buildings, merged markings, instanced props, traffic car meshes (each car is a group ~ 5 meshes × 20 cars = 100 draw calls) maybe use merged car geometry per car (one mesh) with multi-material? Simpler: each car body box + cabin + wheels? Use a merged geometry with vertex colors? Could use InstancedMesh for bodies and cabins separately (2 draw calls) with per-instance transforms updated; wheels skip or instanced. Traffic cars as InstancedMesh body (box), cabin (box), lights? Update instance matrices each frame for 24 cars. Good perf. Colors via instanceColor. Similarly pedestrians instanced (capsule-ish) walking sidewalks? Could skip peds or add simple instanced figures with bobbing.

- Building windows texture generated at 512x512 with lit windows random.
- Neon signs: a handful of planes with emissive canvas text, maybe 12 draw calls, fine.
- Palm trees: instanced trunk cylinders + instanced fronds cones; parks.
- Lamps: instanced pole + glow sprite? Add point lights only a few near player? Point lights expensive. Use emissive lamp heads and no actual light at night, plus ambient. Fine.

Camera:
- Chase camera: target positioned behind bike based on heading and velocity, height 4.2, distance 8.5, lookAt ahead +1.5. Smooth with damping. Add FOV based on speed (65→78) and camera shake on collisions. Slight roll when leaning. Camera collision with buildings? Could clip through; acceptable. Maybe raycast to avoid? skip.
- Start cinematic orbit on title screen? A slow orbit around bike in the city at start; on start transitions to chase. Nice presentation. Implement menu camera orbit with title overlay.

Start screen: overlay with background game render (world visible), big title, controls grid, START button. Auto-start click via capture script (CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR). The capture's startForCapture clicks start selector maybe. Need to check capture-start logic to know how it auto-starts; likely clicks button with text Start/Play. Let me read.

Also capture takes screenshot after 1s; if title screen is shown, screenshot shows title, which is fine but better if auto-start clicks. Let me inspect capture-start.mjs.

name: OpenCode
run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}${{ github.event.issue.title && format(' — {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: Existing issue to run
        required: true
        type: string

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-prepare.yml@3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2
    with:
      runtime_ref: 3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2

  opencode:
    needs: prepare
    if: needs.prepare.outputs.approved == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: read
      pull-requests: write

Let's think through the code in detail before writing, to minimize iteration.

Constants:
GRID = 9 (blocks per side) → block centers at i*SPACING, i from -(G/2)..? Let's set BLOCKS=9, BLOCK=54, ROAD=18, SPACING=72. City outer extent = 9*72 = 648, from -324 to 324. Player starts at intersection near center (0, 0) maybe road along z=0? Road centers at multiples of 72? Let roads at x = k*SPACING for k=-4..4 etc. Intersections at (k*72, j*72). Blocks centered between roads: at ((k+0.5)*72). So block center coordinates ±36, ±108, ... City spans -324..324. Ground plane 1200 with outskirts.

Roads: along x direction (east-west) centered z = k*72, width 18; buildings blocks between. At edges, boundary.

Block content: sidewalk slab from center ±(SPACING-ROAD)/2 = ±27, size 54. Building footprint within block: width/depth up to 44. For park blocks, no building, trees & grass. Maybe 14 parks out of 81. Buildings per block: could be 1 big building, or split into 2-4 smaller ones for variety. This yields more interesting city. For each block, choose a lot pattern (1,2,2x2) with gaps. Each building: footprint and height. Downtown center → heights 40-110; outskirts 8-30. Height function based on distance to center: base 12 + 90 * exp(-dist²/...). Add randomness. Also some iconic tower at center with antenna.

Buildings merged with window texture. Need UV mapping per face scaled: BoxGeometry(width,height,depth). BoxGeometry has material groups per face; merge ignores groups? mergeGeometries with useGroups false merges into one. UV attributes: BoxGeometry UVs each face 0..1. To scale UV per face correctly, we can adjust per-face based on normal:
- For each vertex, look at normal: if |nx| ≈ 1, face is side along z,y → u scale = depth/UNIT, v scale = height/UNIT. If |nz|≈1: u = width/UNIT, v = height/UNIT. If |ny|≈1 (top): u=width, v=depth.
Then uv *= scale. Texture wrapping RepeatWrapping. UNIT = 6 (window tile 6 units). Set texture repeat (1,1) since UVs scaled. Good.
- Top faces should use a roof texture, not windows. Could set uv for top to 0-ish and use a second material? Merged geometry with two materials via groups is possible: build geometry, set groups? Simpler: use one texture that has windows; tops get a roof-ish pattern from texture would look odd. Alternative: separate merged roof mesh (flat boxes) placed on top with dark material. But sides windows texture top face will show windows when viewed from above (rare from chase camera; tall buildings tops invisible mostly, low ones visible). Better: create a material array? mergeGeometries with useGroups true and each box geometry assigned material index? Need groups mapped correctly and material array. BoxGeometry already has 6 groups (material index 0..5). If useGroups false, groups dropped. With useGroups true, groups preserved but indices refer to materials; all boxes use same material array of 6 (right, left, top, bottom, front, back) where top=roof material, others=window material. mergeGeometries with useGroups true should preserve group material indices? It offsets group.start, keeps materialIndex. So create building geometry with material array [windows, windows, roof, roof, windows, windows]. Merging with useGroups true → 2 draw calls with material array? A mesh with groups and material array draws each group separately (many groups = many draw calls!). 150 buildings × 6 groups = 900 draws, bad. Instead merge sides separately from tops? Use two merged geometries: walls (sides only) and roofs (top quads). Build each box's side faces with window material and top face separate with roof material. Merge into 2 meshes. That's clean.

Construct box geometry manually? Use BoxGeometry then delete groups and filter triangles by normal: complex but doable. Easier: build building walls as 4 PlaneGeometry? Use BoxGeometry with groups; extract top face vertices (last 6 vertices? BoxGeometry vertices order: px,nx,py,ny,pz,nz each 4 verts, 6 indices each). We can create walls geometry by taking BoxGeometry and removing the py group (indices 12..17) and ny group? Bottom unseen; keep or remove. Then create top as separate PlaneGeometry rotated. Hmm merging two arrays.

Alternative simpler visually: Use BoxGeometry for building with window texture on all faces including top, but overlay flat roof boxes slightly above each building top with dark gravel/roof material. Also add rooftop details. The window texture on top hidden by roof slab. Roof slab: a box 0.6 tall with dark material, merged. Adds geometry but fine. Let's do walls via full BoxGeometry windows + merged roof caps (dark) + rooftop AC boxes for some. Two merged meshes.

Window texture:
Canvas 512x512: base wall color #6b7280-ish, grid of windows. Each tile 64x64: window rectangle inset, random brightness. Texture tile = 6x6 world units? Set UNIT = 5. Windows ~ each 2.5 wide? Tile 5 units gives 1 window per 5m. Fine. Include some lit windows (warm). Use map and emissiveMap with same texture? Emissive map would glow walls too. Instead generate separate emissive canvas with black background and only windows drawn (some lit), and use as emissiveMap. That gives night windows glow. Use two textures, same UVs. Nice. But material color tint via vertex colors? Merged mesh can't per-instance color but can use vertex colors per building: set color attribute for each box vertices; material.vertexColors = true. Then map multiplied by color. Nice variety: tints light gray, beige, cool gray. Window texture should be fairly neutral and color multiplies including window color (emissive unaffected by vertex color? emissiveMap * emissive color, not vertex color; lit windows stay warm). Good.

Material:
MeshStandardMaterial({ map: windowMap, emissiveMap: windowEmissive, emissive: 0xffc27a, emissiveIntensity: nightFactor, vertexColors: true, roughness: .75, metalness: .15 }).
At dusk increase emissiveIntensity.

Buildings collision boxes: AABB list per building {minX,maxX,minZ,maxZ}. Player collision circle radius ~0.7. Resolve by finding nearest point; push out; reflect velocity component; damage.

Parks: 10 blocks with grass slab (green), low hedges? Trees. Maybe a central park near center. Represent slab at y=0.2 with grass color and trees (instanced). Add path? optional.

Ground layout:
- Base plane huge 1600x1600, material dark asphalt with slight roughness. Add a subtle noise texture generated canvas (asphalt) repeated 200 times. This texture helps visual richness. Use canvas 256 noise gray; RepeatWrapping repeat 160. With anisotropy 4.
- Sidewalk slabs: merged boxes (54×0.3×54) at each block, concrete color with grid texture? Add a concrete texture canvas with cracks/tiles; apply repeat per block via UV? Could reuse map repeated. Each slab is BoxGeometry with UV default; texture repeats maybe 8×8 via texture repeat globally; but for merged different slabs, repeat same per face fine (each slab face 0-1 → 8 tiles). Good.

Pole cylinder geometry (0.12 radius, 5.5 tall), head box/sphere. InstancedMesh with 2 draw calls. Add PointLights? no. - Cars: InstancedMesh body boxes + cabin boxes + maybe headlights/taillights as emissive instanced small boxes. 4 draw calls. 28 cars. Cars drive along roads (horizontal/vertical), loop at city bounds, stop? Keep flowing, turn at random intersections occasionally. Implement simple lane paths: each car has axis ('x' or 'z'), lane offset ±4.5 (right-hand traffic: for axis x, direction +1, z = lane +4.5? Let's just lane +4.5), pos, speed 8-16. Choose direction; wrap at ±340. At intersections maybe change lane direction with probability when near intersection. Traffic driving straight through intersections is fine.

Collision with player: AABB approximation; if distance < 2.2, push player, reduce speed, sparks, heat +. Cars get knocked slightly? Keep them moving. Add a little bounce.

Cars headlights at night: emissive boxes on front, and two SpotLights? Too expensive. Use emissive + glow points maybe. Maybe add cone light pools? skip.

Pedestrians:
- Instanced capsules? Use simple low-poly person: cylinder body + sphere head, instanced separately, ~40 walking on sidewalks, bobbing. 3 draw calls. Colors per instance. They walk along sidewalk edges and flee when bike near (increase speed away). Hitting them → heat +, small speed loss, "OOF" sound; maybe not gore. Add to chaos. Could avoid contact by their dodge. Their collision circle radius 0.5; on hit, set knocked state (lay down?) Simpler: they dive away (position offset + opacity?), then respawn after 10s. Instanced matrices update; play a yelp. Police:
- At heat >= 2, spawn cop bike at 100 units away. Cop model similar to player but black/white with flashing red-blue lights. AI: steer toward player, accelerate; contact → "BUSTED" ends contract, respawn at nearest intersection, lose heat. Or health damage per second within radius. Let's do damage on contact then cop backs off. Wanted decreases over time if no chaos. Simpler: Wanted stars from chaos, police chase when >=3; contact causes health -, screen flash. If wrecked, respawn. This is optional but fun. Implementation moderate: reuse bike mesh factory, separate simple update steering.

- Checkpoint: glowing torus ring vertical? Delivery gates: torus radius 3 rotated to face along route, with beam cylinder, arrow on minimap. Pass through within 4 units. Spawn at random intersection at least 80 units away. 60s timer per target, cash +150 × multiplier, multiplier increases each consecutive, timer resets and reduces slightly. After 10 deliveries "contract complete" +$2000 and restart. HUD shows "DELIVERY 3/10" and countdown.

Implement 3D arrow sprite/chevron that rotates above bike? Could be visually distracting. Use a small floating icon + ring visible. Minimap enough, plus a tall light beam at checkpoint (visible over buildings, hot pink) — great. Beam cylinder 60 tall with additive gradient texture.
- Checkpoint gate torus at y=2.5, rotates slowly, pulsing emissive.

function addBox(list, w, h, d, x, y, z, color = null) {
  const geo = new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, h, d)
  if (color) paintGeometry(geo, color)
  geo.translate(x, y, z)
  list.push(geo)
}

const SIGN_TEXTS = [
  ['NEON RIDER', '#31e6ff', 'SUNSET CITY'],
  ['24/7', '#ff3ba7', 'OPEN ALL NIGHT'],
  ['TURBO', '#ffb020', 'MOTOR CO.'],
  ['OMG FM', '#b06bff', '98.3 MHz'],
  ['MOTEL', '#ff5470', 'VACANCY'],
  ['PIZZA', '#ffcf4d', 'SLICE THE NIGHT'],
  ['VICE', '#ff3ba7', 'BEACH CLUB'],
  ['SUNSET', '#31e6ff', 'BLVD 09'],
  ['HANZO', '#8dffb5', 'NOODLE BAR'],
  ['NEON', '#ff7a45', 'ARCADE'],
  ['CHROME', '#7ddcff', 'CYCLE WORKS'],
  ['NIGHT', '#ff4d9d', 'SHIFT'],
]

function signCanvas(label, main, sub) {
  const W = 1024
  const H = 384
  const canvas = document.createElement('canvas')
  canvas.width = W
  canvas.height = H
  const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d')
  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, W, H)
  ctx.shadowColor = main
  ctx.shadowBlur = 34
  ctx.strokeStyle = main
  ctx.lineWidth = 9
  ctx.strokeRect(26, 26, W - 52, H - 52)
  ctx.globalAlpha = 0.75
  ctx.strokeStyle = '#ffffff'
  ctx.lineWidth = 2
  ctx.strokeRect(40, 40, W - 80, H - 80)
  ctx.globalAlpha = 1
  ctx.font = '700 40px "Trebuchet MS", sans-serif'
  ctx.fillStyle = '#ffffff'
  ctx.textAlign = 'left'
  ctx.textBaseline = 'middle'
  ctx.fillText(sub.toUpperCase(), 64, 100)
  ctx.fillStyle = main
  ctx.shadowBlur = 46
  let size = 150
  ctx.font = `italic 900 ${size}px "Arial Black", Impact, sans-serif`
  while (ctx.measureText(label).width > W - 130 && size > 54) {
    size -= 6
    ctx.font = `italic 900 ${size}px "Arial Black", Impact, sans-serif`
  }
  ctx.fillText(label, 62, 224)
  ctx.shadowBlur = 18
  ctx.fillStyle = main
  ctx.fillRect(62, 306, 300, 5)
  ctx.fillStyle = '#ffe9b8'
  ctx.beginPath()
  ctx.arc(946, 88, 12, 0, Math.PI * 2)
  ctx.fill()
  return makeTexture(canvas)
}

export function makeGlowTexture() {
  const [canvas, ctx] = canvas2d(128)
  const grad = ctx.createRadialGradient(64, 64, 0, 64, 64, 64)
  grad.addColorStop(0, 'rgba(255,255,255,1)')
  grad.addColorStop(0.25, 'rgba(255,255,255,.7)')
  grad.addColorStop(0.55, 'rgba(255,255,255,.18)')
  grad.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(255,255,255,0)')
  ctx.fillStyle = grad
  ctx.fillRect(0, 0, 128, 128)
  const tex = new THREE.CanvasTexture(canvas)
  tex.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace
  return tex
}

const PARK_BLOCKS = new Set(['2,6', '6,2', '4,7', '7,4', '1,1', '7,7', '1,6', '6,1'])
const PALETTE = ['#b9c1cc', '#a5aebc', '#cfc4b4', '#98a4b4', '#c4b4a4', '#8b97a9', '#d4cfc5']
const NEON_COLORS = ['#31e6ff', '#ff3ba7', '#ffb020', '#8dffb5', '#b06bff', '#ff7a45']

export class GameAudio {
  constructor() {
    this.ctx = null
    this.muted = false
    this.ready = false
  }

  start() {
    if (this.ctx) {
      if (this.ctx.state === 'suspended') this.ctx.resume()
      return
    }
    const Ctx = window.AudioContext || window.webkitAudioContext
    if (!Ctx) return
    try {
      const ctx = new Ctx()
      this.ctx = ctx
      this.master = ctx.createGain()
      this.master.gain.value = this.muted ? 0 : 0.5
      const comp = ctx.createDynamicsCompressor()
      comp.threshold.value = -18
      comp.knee.value = 24
      comp.ratio.value = 6
      this.master.connect(comp)
      comp.connect(ctx.destination)

      const noiseBuffer = ctx.createBuffer(1, ctx.sampleRate * 2, ctx.sampleRate)
      const data = noiseBuffer.getChannelData(0)
      for (let i = 0; i < data.length; i++) data[i] = Math.random() * 2 - 1
      this.noiseBuffer = noiseBuffer

      this.engineGain = ctx.createGain()
      this.engineGain.gain.value = 0
      this.engineFilter = ctx.createBiquadFilter()
      this.engineFilter.type = 'lowpass'
      this.engineFilter.frequency.value = 500
      this.engineFilter.Q.value = 1.1
      this.engineFilter.connect(this.engineGain)
      this.engineGain.connect(this.master)

      this.osc1 = ctx.createOscillator()
      this.osc1.type = 'sawtooth'
      this.osc1.frequency.value = 52
      this.osc2 = ctx.createOscillator()
      this.osc2.type = 'sawtooth'
      this.osc2.frequency.value = 52.6
      this.osc2.detune.value = 8
      this.sub = ctx.createOscillator()
      this.sub.type = 'square'
      this.sub.frequency.value = 26
      const subGain = ctx.createGain()
      subGain.gain.value = 0.35
      this.osc1.connect(this.engineFilter)
      this.osc2.connect(this.engineFilter)
      this.sub.connect(subGain)
      subGain.connect(this.engineFilter)
      this.osc1.start()
      this.osc2.start()
      this.sub.start()

      const wind = ctx.createBufferSource()
      wind.buffer = noiseBuffer
      wind.loop = true
      const windFilter = ctx.createBiquadFilter()
      windFilter.type = 'bandpass'
      windFilter.frequency.value = 900
      windFilter.Q.value = 0.6
      this.windGain = ctx.createGain()
      this.windGain.gain.value = 0
      wind.connect(windFilter)
      windFilter.connect(this.windGain)
      this.windGain.connect(this.master)
      wind.start()

      const tire = ctx.createBufferSource()
      tire.buffer = noiseBuffer
      tire.loop = true
      const tireFilter = ctx.createBiquadFilter()
      tireFilter.type = 'highpass'
      tireFilter.frequency.value = 2600
      this.tireGain = ctx.createGain()
      this.tireGain.gain.value = 0
      tire.connect(tireFilter)
      tireFilter.connect(this.tireGain)
      this.tireGain.connect(this.master)
      tire.start()

      this.siren = ctx.createOscillator()
      this.siren.type = 'triangle'
      this.siren.frequency.value = 780
      this.sirenGain = ctx.createGain()
      this.sirenGain.gain.value = 0
      this.siren.connect(this.sirenGain)
      this.sirenGain.connect(this.master)
      this.siren.start()

      this.ready = true
      if (ctx.state === 'suspended') ctx.resume()
    } catch {
      this.ready = false
    }
  }

  setMuted(muted) {
    this.muted = muted
    if (!this.ctx) return
    this.master.gain.setTargetAtTime(muted ? 0 : 0.5, this.ctx.currentTime, 0.05)
  }

  update(ratio, drifting, wanted, copDistance) {
    if (!this.ctx || !this.ready) return
    const now = this.ctx.currentTime
    const freq = 46 + ratio * 162
    this.osc1.frequency.setTargetAtTime(freq, now, 0.06)
    this.osc2.frequency.setTargetAtTime(freq * 1.012, now, 0.06)
    this.sub.frequency.setTargetAtTime(freq * 0.5, now, 0.08)
    this.engineFilter.frequency.setTargetAtTime(360 + ratio * 1900, now, 0.08)
    this.engineGain.gain.setTargetAtTime(0.022 + ratio * 0.055, now, 0.1)
    this.windGain.gain.setTargetAtTime(Math.pow(ratio, 1.7) * 0.16, now, 0.12)
    this.tireGain.gain.setTargetAtTime(drifting ? 0.12 : 0, now, 0.06)
    if (this.sirenGain) {
      const active = wanted >= 3
      const near = Math.max(0, 1 - (copDistance ?? 999) / 140)
      this.sirenGain.gain.setTargetAtTime(active ? 0.018 + near * 0.045 : 0, now, 0.2)
      if (active) {
        const flip = Math.sin(now * 7.4) > 0 ? 690 : 980
        this.siren.frequency.setTargetAtTime(flip, now, 0.03)
      }
    }
  }

  crash(strength = 1) {
    if (!this.ctx || !this.ready) return
    const now = this.ctx.currentTime
    const src = this.ctx.createBufferSource()
    src.buffer = this.noiseBuffer
    const filter = this.ctx.createBiquadFilter()
    filter.type = 'lowpass'
    filter.frequency.value = 1200
    const gain = this.ctx.createGain()
    const vol = Math.min(0.4, 0.1 + strength * 0.025)
    gain.gain.setValueAtTime(vol, now)
    gain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, now + 0.45)
    src.connect(filter)
    filter.connect(gain)
    gain.connect(this.master)
    src.start(now)
    src.stop(now + 0.5)

    const thump = this.ctx.createOscillator()
    const thumpGain = this.ctx.createGain()
    thump.type = 'sine'
    thump.frequency.setValueAtTime(90, now)
    thump.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(38, now + 0.25)
    thumpGain.gain.setValueAtTime(vol * 0.9, now)
    thumpGain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, now + 0.3)
    thump.connect(thumpGain)
    thumpGain.connect(this.master)
    thump.start(now)
    thump.stop(now + 0.32)
  }

  pickup() {
    if (!this.ctx || !this.ready) return
    const now = this.ctx.currentTime
    ;[660, 880, 1175].forEach((f, i) => {
      const osc = this.ctx.createOscillator()
      const gain = this.ctx.createGain()
      osc.type = 'sine'
      osc.frequency.value = f
      gain.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, now + i * 0.07)
      gain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.16, now + i * 0.07 + 0.01)
      gain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, now + i * 0.07 + 0.22)
      osc.connect(gain)
      gain.connect(this.master)
      osc.start(now + i * 0.07)
      osc.stop(now + i * 0.07 + 0.25)
    })
  }

  yelp() {
    if (!this.ctx || !this.ready) return
    const now = this.ctx.currentTime
    const osc = this.ctx.createOscillator()
    const gain = this.ctx.createGain()
    osc.type = 'square'
    osc.frequency.setValueAtTime(420, now)
    osc.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(210, now + 0.18)
    gain.gain.setValueAtTime(0.03, now)
    gain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, now + 0.2)
    osc.connect(gain)
    gain.connect(this.master)
    osc.start(now)
    osc.stop(now + 0.22)
  }
}

import * as THREE from 'three'

const clamp = THREE.MathUtils.clamp

export class Hud {
  constructor(world) {
    this.world = world
    this.el = {
      hud: document.getElementById('hud'),
      cash: document.getElementById('cash'),
      stars: document.getElementById('stars'),
      starItems: Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('#stars i')),
      missionLabel: document.getElementById('missionLabel'),
      timer: document.getElementById('timer'),
      timerFill: document.getElementById('timerFill'),
      distance: document.getElementById('distance'),
      multiplier: document.getElementById('multiplier'),
      healthFill: document.getElementById('healthFill'),
      boostFill: document.getElementById('boostFill'),
      zone: document.getElementById('zone'),
      timeChip: document.getElementById('timeChip'),
      toast: document.getElementById('toast'),
      toastTitle: document.getElementById('toastTitle'),
      toastSub: document.getElementById('toastSub'),
      flash: document.getElementById('fx-flash'),
      speedFx: document.getElementById('fx-speed'),
      muteBtn: document.getElementById('muteBtn'),
      speedo: document.getElementById('speedo'),
      minimap: document.getElementById('minimap'),
    }
    this.mapCtx = this.el.minimap.getContext('2d')
    this.speedoCtx = this.el.speedo.getContext('2d')
    this.cashValue = 0
    this.heatValue = -1
    this.mapAcc = 1
    this.speedoAcc = 1
    this.toastTimeout = null
    this.base = document.createElement('canvas')
    this.base.width = this.base.height = 512
    this.mapScale = 512 / 720
    this.drawBase()
    this.muteBtn = this.el.muteBtn
  }

  drawBase() {
    const ctx = this.base.getContext('2d')
    const S = 512
    const scale = this.mapScale
    const toX = (x) => (x + 360) * scale
    const toY = (z) => (z + 360) * scale
    ctx.fillStyle = '#081019'
    ctx.fillRect(0, 0, S, S)
    const grad = ctx.createRadialGradient(S / 2, S / 2, 30, S / 2, S / 2, 280)
    grad.addColorStop(0, 'rgba(31,58,80,.25)')
    grad.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(0,0,0,0)')
    ctx.fillStyle = grad
    ctx.fillRect(0, 0, S, S)

    // roads
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#233345'
    ctx.lineWidth = 3
    for (const c of THREE.MathUtils ? this.world.roadCenters : []) {
      ctx.beginPath()
      ctx.moveTo(toX(c), 8)
      ctx.lineTo(toX(c), S - 8)
      ctx.stroke()
      ctx.beginPath()
      ctx.moveTo(8, toY(c))
      ctx.lineTo(S - 8, toY(c))
      ctx.stroke()
    }

    for (const b of this.world.mapBlocks) {
      const w = 58 * scale
      const h = 58 * scale
      ctx.fillStyle = b.park ? '#153a29' : '#111e2b'
      ctx.fillRect(toX(b.x) - w / 2, toY(b.z) - h / 2, w, h)
      ctx.strokeStyle = b.park ? 'rgba(77,191,162,.25)' : 'rgba(49,230,255,.08)'
      ctx.lineWidth = 1
      ctx.strokeRect(toX(b.x) - w / 2, toY(b.z) - h / 2, w, h)
    }

    ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(49,230,255,.3)'
    ctx.lineWidth = 2
    ctx.strokeRect(4, 4, S - 8, S - 8)
    ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(49,230,255,.5)'
    ctx.font = '700 11px "DejaVu Sans Mono", monospace'
    ctx.fillText('N', S / 2 - 4, 16)
  }

  setStarted(started) {
    this.el.hud.classList.toggle('hidden', !started)
  }

  setTime(name) {
    this.el.timeChip.textContent = name.toUpperCase()
    this.el.timeChip.style.color = name === 'night' ? '#ffb3da' : name === 'day' ? '#ffe9b8' : '#bfeaff'
  }

  setMuted(muted) {
    this.el.muteBtn.textContent = muted ? '×' : '♪'
    this.el.muteBtn.classList.toggle('off', muted)
  }

  toast(title, sub = '', tone = '', duration = 2.4) {
    this.el.toastTitle.textContent = title
    this.el.toastSub.textContent = sub
    this.el.toast.className = `toast ${tone}`
    void this.el.toast.offsetWidth
    this.el.toast.classList.add('show')
    clearTimeout(this.toastTimeout)
    this.toastTimeout = setTimeout(() => this.el.toast.classList.remove('show'), duration * 1000)
  }

  flash(strength = 0.5) {
    const el = this.el.flash
    el.style.transition = 'none'
    el.style.opacity = String(strength)
    void el.offsetWidth
    el.style.transition = 'opacity .5s ease-out'
    el.style.opacity = '0'
  }

  setSpeedFx(ratio) {
    this.el.speedFx.style.opacity = String(clamp((ratio - 0.55) * 1.2, 0, 0.55))
  }

  update(state, dt) {
    if (Math.floor(state.cash) !== Math.floor(this.cashValue)) {
      this.cashValue = state.cash
      this.el.cash.textContent = '$' + Math.max(0, Math.floor(state.cash)).toLocaleString('en-US')
    }

    const wanted = Math.min(5, Math.floor(state.heat + 0.08))
    if (wanted !== this.heatValue) {
      this.heatValue = wanted
      this.el.starItems.forEach((item, i) => item.classList.toggle('on', i < wanted))
      this.el.stars.classList.toggle('hot', wanted >= 3)
    }

    this.el.missionLabel.textContent = `DELIVERY ${String(state.delivery + 1).padStart(2, '0')} / 10`
    this.el.timer.textContent = Math.max(0, state.missionTime).toFixed(1)
    this.el.timer.classList.toggle('low', state.missionTime < 10)
    this.el.timerFill.style.transform = `scaleX(${clamp(state.missionTime / state.missionMax, 0, 1)})`
    this.el.timerFill.classList.toggle('low', state.missionTime < 10)
    this.el.distance.textContent = String(Math.round(state.distance))
    this.el.multiplier.textContent = `PAYOUT x${state.multiplier.toFixed(1)}`

    this.el.healthFill.style.width = `${clamp(state.health, 0, 100)}%`
    this.el.healthFill.classList.toggle('low', state.health < 30)
    this.el.boostFill.style.width = `${clamp(state.boost, 0, 100)}%`

    const zone = Math.abs(state.pos.x) < 115 && Math.abs(state.pos.z) < 135
      ? 'DOWNTOWN'
      : state.pos.z < -110 ? 'NORTH SHORE' : state.pos.z > 110 ? 'SOUTH BEACH' : state.pos.x > 0 ? 'EAST SIDE' : 'WEST END'
    if (this.el.zone.textContent !== zone) this.el.zone.textContent = zone

    this.setSpeedFx(clamp(state.speed / 60, 0, 1))

    this.mapAcc += dt
    if (this.mapAcc > 0.075) {
      this.mapAcc = 0
      this.drawMinimap(state)
    }

    if (this.speedoAcc > 0.04) {
      this.speedoAcc = 0

  drawMinimap(state) {
    const ctx = this.mapCtx
    const S = 512
    const scale = this.mapScale
    const toX = (x) => (x + 360) * scale
    const toY = (z) => (z + 360) * scale
    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, S, S)
    ctx.drawImage(this.base, 0, 0)
    const px = toX(state.pos.x)
    const py = toY(state.pos.z)

    if (state.target) {
      const tx = toX(state.target.x)
      const ty = toY(state.target.z)
      ctx.save()
      ctx.setLineDash([5, 9])
      ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255,59,167,.32)'
      ctx.lineWidth = 2
      ctx.beginPath()
      ctx.moveTo(px, py)
      ctx.lineTo(tx, ty)
      ctx.stroke()
      ctx.setLineDash([])
      const pulse = 1 + Math.sin(state.time * 4) * 0.12
      ctx.translate(tx, ty)
      ctx.rotate(Math.PI / 4)
      ctx.shadowColor = '#ff3ba7'
      ctx.shadowBlur = 18
      ctx.fillStyle = '#ff6fbe'
      ctx.fillRect(-6 * pulse, -6 * pulse, 12 * pulse, 12 * pulse)
      ctx.restore()
      ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255,59,167,.35)'
      ctx.lineWidth = 2
      ctx.beginPath()
      ctx.arc(tx, ty, 13 + Math.sin(state.time * 4) * 3, 0, Math.PI * 2)
      ctx.stroke()
    }

    if (state.cars) {
      ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(155,176,196,.55)'
      for (const car of state.cars) {
        ctx.fillRect(toX(car.x) - 1.5, toY(car.z) - 1.5, 3, 3)
      }
    }

    if (state.cops) {
      state.cops.forEach((cop, i) => {
        ctx.fillStyle = i % 2 === 0 ? '#ff4455' : '#5599ff'
        ctx.shadowColor = ctx.fillStyle
        ctx.shadowBlur = 8
        ctx.beginPath()
        ctx.arc(toX(cop.x), toY(cop.z), 4, 0, Math.PI * 2)
        ctx.fill()
        ctx.shadowBlur = 0
      })
    }

    const fx = Math.sin(state.yaw)
    const fy = Math.cos(state.yaw)
    const sideX = -fy
    const sideY = fx
    ctx.save()
    ctx.translate(px, py)
    ctx.shadowColor = '#31e6ff'
    ctx.shadowBlur = 16
    ctx.fillStyle = '#a9f8ff'
    ctx.beginPath()
    ctx.moveTo(fx * 13, fy * 13)
    ctx.lineTo(-fx * 8 + sideX * 7, -fy * 8 + sideY * 7)
    ctx.lineTo(-fx * 8 - sideX * 7, -fy * 8 - sideY * 7)
    ctx.closePath()
    ctx.fill()
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#ffffff'
    ctx.lineWidth = 1.5
    ctx.stroke()
    ctx.restore()
  }

  drawSpeedo(kmh, boost, boosting) {
    const ctx = this.speedoCtx
    const S = 320
    const cx = S / 2
    const cy = S / 2 + 4
    const R = 118
    const start = Math.PI * 0.75
    const end = Math.PI * 2.25
    const range = end - start
    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, S, S)

    ctx.beginPath()
    ctx.arc(cx, cy, R + 18, 0, Math.PI * 2)
    ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(4,9,16,.52)'
    ctx.fill()
    ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,.08)'
    ctx.lineWidth = 1
    ctx.stroke()

    ctx.beginPath()
    ctx.arc(cx, cy, R, start, end)
    ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,.09)'
    ctx.lineWidth = 11
    ctx.lineCap = 'round'
    ctx.stroke()

    for (let v = 0; v <= 240; v += 20) {
      const a = start + (v / 240) * range
      const major = v % 60 === 0
      const r1 = R - (major ? 20 : 14)
      const r2 = R - 7
      ctx.beginPath()
      ctx.moveTo(cx + Math.cos(a) * r1, cy + Math.sin(a) * r1)
      ctx.lineTo(cx + Math.cos(a) * r2, cy + Math.sin(a) * r2)
      ctx.strokeStyle = major ? 'rgba(255,255,255,.45)' : 'rgba(255,255,255,.16)'
      ctx.lineWidth = major ? 2 : 1
      ctx.stroke()
      if (major) {
        ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(174,203,220,.6)'
        ctx.font = '600 11px "DejaVu Sans Mono", monospace'
        ctx.textAlign = 'center'
        ctx.textBaseline = 'middle'
        ctx.fillText(String(v), cx + Math.cos(a) * (R - 37), cy + Math.sin(a) * (R - 37))
      }
    }

    const frac = clamp(kmh / 240, 0, 1)
    if (frac > 0.003) {
      const grad = ctx.createLinearGradient(cx - R, cy + R, cx + R, cy - R)
      grad.addColorStop(0, '#31e6ff')
      grad.addColorStop(0.62, '#8df7ff')
      grad.addColorStop(0.86, '#ff3ba7')
      grad.addColorStop(1, '#ff7a45')
      ctx.save()
      ctx.shadowColor = frac > 0.8 ? '#ff3ba7' : '#31e6ff'
      ctx.shadowBlur = 20
      ctx.beginPath()
      ctx.arc(cx, cy, R, start, start + frac * range)
      ctx.strokeStyle = grad
      ctx.lineWidth = 11
      ctx.stroke()
      ctx.restore()
      const a = start + frac * range
      ctx.beginPath()
      ctx.arc(cx + Math.cos(a) * R, cy + Math.sin(a) * R, 5, 0, Math.PI * 2)
      ctx.fillStyle = '#ffffff'
      ctx.shadowColor = '#8df7ff'
      ctx.shadowBlur = 14
      ctx.fill()
      ctx.shadowBlur = 0
    }

    ctx.textAlign = 'center'
    ctx.textBaseline = 'middle'
    ctx.fillStyle = '#f4fdff'
    ctx.shadowColor = 'rgba(49,230,255,.55)'
    ctx.shadowBlur = 18
    ctx.font = 'italic 900 58px "Arial Black", Impact, sans-serif'
    ctx.fillText(String(Math.round(kmh)), cx, cy - 6)
    ctx.shadowBlur = 0
    ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(160,198,218,.75)'
    ctx.font = '600 11px "DejaVu Sans Mono", monospace'
    ctx.letterSpacing = '2px'
    ctx.fillText('KM/H', cx, cy + 30)

    ctx.beginPath()
    ctx.arc(cx, cy, R + 9, start, end)
    ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(49,230,255,.18)'
    ctx.lineWidth = 3
    ctx.stroke()
    if (boost > 1) {
      const ba = start + (boost / 100) * range
      ctx.beginPath()
      ctx.arc(cx, cy, R + 9, start, ba)
      ctx.strokeStyle = boosting ? '#ff3ba7' : 'rgba(255,59,167,.5)'
      ctx.lineWidth = 3
      ctx.stroke()
    }
  }
}

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

I have completed the development of the **GTA-style 3D open-world motorcycle game** with the following achievements:

## 🎮 Core Gameplay Features Implemented
- **Procedural city generation** with 9×9 blocks, varied building heights, parks, and traffic
- **Motorcycle physics** with acceleration, drifting, boosting, steering, and collision detection
- **Police AI** with wanted-level system and dynamic chase behavior
- **Delivery missions** with timing, cash payouts, and multipliers
- **HUD elements**: minimap, speedometer, health, boost, stars, and interactive panels
- **Audio system** with wind, tire, siren, and impact sounds

## 🎨 Visual & UI Enhancements
- **Improved camera framing** for better bike visibility and composition
- **Dynamic lighting** with day/night presets (toggle with `T`)
- **Enhanced UI layout** and responsive design (mobile 390×844 layout tested)
- **Touch controls** for mobile gameplay
- **Particle effects** for sparks, smoke, and neon signs
- **Menu screens** with professional branding and instruction overlays

## 🛠️ Development Improvements
- **Fixed visual issues** in `main.js` (camera distance, FOV, gate glow)
- **Optimized city aesthetics** in `world.js` (day preset, better sky)
- **Enhanced UI styling** in `style.css` (mobile touch controls, layout tweaks)
- **Added runtime helpers**: capture scripts for automated testing

## 🧪 Verification Completed
- ✅ **Start auto-click** validated via runtime capture (desktop + mobile)
- ✅ **Console checks**: No runtime errors or failed same-origin requests
- ✅ **Driving tests**: Throttle, steering, boost, drift, collisions, delivery pickup confirmed
- ✅ **Pause/resume**, **wreck/respawn**, **time cycles**, **mobile layout** screenshots captured
- ✅ **Build success** with Vite + Three.js 0.180.0

## 📁 Repository Commit
All source files, documentation, and final screenshots are now committed:
- `src/` – complete game code
- `index.html`, `package.json`, `.gitignore`, runtime helpers
- `screenshots/` – menu previews, gameplay capture, final desktop/mobile outputs

The game is ready for deployment with **automatic start button detection**, full **Playwright verification**, and a polished **GTA-inspired riding experience** in Sunset City.

Let me know if you need any further adjustments or additional features! 🚀
